success_patterns: Four of the eight clues (Baden-Powell, Mae West, SCTV, Love Story) appear verbatim in a J! Archive or TriviaBistro line. The agent used that hit to anchor on the right entity. It kept the archive's own form ('Lord Robert Baden-Powell'). Two of these snippets were truncated right after the clue, and the answer came from other passages that repeatedly paired the clue's named entities.

For 'this <type>' clues, the agent answered the category noun and ignored the named anchors in the clue. 'Elizabeth Spencer... in this country' gave Italy, not a region or the novel. 'One of these spiritual leaders' gave Dalai Lama, not Tenzin Gyatso. 'This talk show host's favorite recipes' in 'In the Kitchen with Rosie' gave Oprah Winfrey, not the co-author Rosie. 'This lively dance' gave Polka.

The answers were short and in the standard form: 'SCTV' without 'Network' (the clue's quoted word 'network' was dropped), 'Polka' with no article, and full first-plus-last names for real people ('Oprah Winfrey', 'Mae West'). Quoted words in the clue were treated as hints, not as part of the answer.

When a work's title appears in quotation marks in the clue, the agent took the answer from the person or entity the passages attach to the work through a subtitle, possessive or byline ('Oprah's Favorite Recipes'). It did not use a name inside the title.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers verbatim archive hits, truncated snippets, type-matching, quoted-word hints and head-noun dropping. Earlier attempts to add a mandatory check line or to rewrite old rules regressed the score, so I am not touching that. The one habit that is not explicit is how to pick the answer when a clue names a work by its title in quotes ('In the Kitchen with Rosie'). A name inside that title (Rosie) is a decoy, and the real link is the subtitle, possessive or byline in the passages. This pattern fits the observed successes and is low-risk, because it only tells the agent which of the passage's entities to choose.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - A work's title in quotation marks inside the clue ('the bestseller "In the Kitchen with Rosie"') is an anchor. A name inside the title ('Rosie') is not the answer. Find the passage line that ties the title to the entity the clue wants, such as a subtitle, possessive or byline ('Oprah's Favorite Recipes', 'by Erich Segal'). Answer with that entity, in the full standard form the passages repeat ('Oprah Winfrey').
